svg.title: DGX Spark nested Kubernetes lab: MacBook terminal, kubeadm root cluster, two vClusters
svg.desc: A MacBook on the home LAN is the terminal. It reaches the root cluster API on 192.168.0.100:6443, the dev-lab vCluster API on 192.168.0.111 and the llms vCluster API on 192.168.0.112. Outside the Spark, sema01 runs every Ansible playbook through Semaphore: it gets a 15-minute SSH certificate from vault01 and logs in to the Spark as svc-ansible. On the DGX Spark, the kubeadm root cluster owns the node, Cilium, MetalLB, the GPU Operator with 15 time-slices, storage and Prometheus. Each vCluster runs its own API server, controller-manager, CoreDNS and SQLite as pods in a root namespace, and a syncer copies its pods, Services and PVCs to the root, where the root scheduler places them on the single node. Budgets: dev-lab 2 CPU, 8 Gi, 2 slices; llms 4 CPU, 48 Gi, 8 slices; the root keeps 14 CPU, about 64 GiB and 5 slices.
svg.text: home LAN 192.168.0.0/24 · the MacBook is only a client
all three clusters and every GPU slice live on this box
budget 2 CPU · 8 Gi · 2 GPU slices · 300 Gi — tenants & experiments
its own control plane — runs as pods in root namespace vc-dev-lab
copies pods · Services · PVCs down to the root as <name>-x-<ns>-x-<vc>
budget 4 CPU · 48 Gi · 8 GPU slices · 500 Gi — serving & training
its own control plane — runs as pods in root namespace vc-llms
copies pods · Services · PVCs down to the root as <name>-x-<ns>-x-<vc>

g.text: dgx-spark-1 is control plane AND worker · owns node, network, storage, GPU · keeps 14 CPU · ~64 GiB · 5 slices
node dgx-spark-1: kubelet · kube-proxy · containerd + NVIDIA runtime
every pod of all three clusters really runs here — e.g. vllm-…-x-llm-serving-x-llms in namespace vc-llms
vc-dev-lab and vc-llms each hold one vCluster: its control-plane pods, its synced workload pods, and a ResourceQuota (the hard budget)
plus a Cilium policy that keeps the two vClusters from talking to each other. Inner quotas are ceilings; the root quota is the real cap.
Requests from tenants pass two API servers: first the vCluster's (their RBAC, quotas, policies), then — via the syncer — the root's.

svg.text: syncers talk only to the root API (scoped ServiceAccount token)

g.text: DGX OS 7 (Ubuntu 24.04) · NVIDIA driver + CUDA · Docker (shares containerd) · AppArmor · swap off
hardware — shared by everything above; the root cluster's quotas decide who gets how much

svg.text: Semaphore: ssh :22 as svc-ansible + 15-min cert · kubectl/helm :6443
How the hardware is split (hard caps, enforced by ResourceQuotas in the root cluster)
